stem:
Esha looks at the diagram. Rays $OX$ and $OY$ meet at $O$ and form $\angle XOY$. A full turn around $O$ is divided into $360$ equal parts.

Which claim correctly assigns a degree measure to $\angle XOY$?

options.text: The measure of $\angle XOY$ is the number of those equal one-degree parts that fit in the turn from ray $OX$ to ray $OY$.
Report the words one-degree unit as the measure of $\angle XOY$.
Count any parts of a full turn between the arms, even when those parts are not equal.
The degree number written for $\angle XOY$ produces the equal parts of the full turn, so she starts from a chosen number and then splits the turn.

teacher.key_rationale: A degree measure counts how many equal one-degree parts of a full turn sit between the arms. Naming the unit label, counting unequal parts, or starting from a written degree number to invent the split all miss that hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as rays OX and OY meeting at O with an angle arc.
